CORRECTION TO A CLAIM IN scripts/hooks/pre-commit AND IN CLAUDE.md: a merge commit CAN fire pre-commit, and it is the dangerous case that does. The header of scripts/hooks/pre-commit says in capitals that NONE OF THIS RUNS ON A MERGE COMMIT, and CLAUDE.md repeats it as verified -- a fast-forward creates no commit and fires no hook, a true merge commit fires pre-merge-commit and never pre-commit. The second half is incomplete. MEASURED just now absorbing 47 commits of main into campaign/the-escapement: the merge CONFLICTED on three files, I resolved them by hand, and On branch campaign/the-escapement
Your branch is ahead of 'origin/main' by 13 commits.
  (use "git push" to publish your local commits)

nothing to commit, working tree clean to conclude the merge RAN THE FULL GATE -- fmt, clippy, type-audit, and all three subfloor chunks, 3302 tests, rc=0, wall 50.1s. There is no pre-merge-commit hook in scripts/hooks at all (the directory holds exactly post-merge, pre-commit, pre-push), so by elimination it was pre-commit. The distinction that matters: git runs pre-merge-commit for an AUTOMATIC merge commit, but a conflicted merge that stops for resolution and is concluded with an explicit On branch campaign/the-escapement
Your branch is ahead of 'origin/main' by 13 commits.
  (use "git push" to publish your local commits)

nothing to commit, working tree clean is an ordinary commit invocation and fires pre-commit like any other. WHY THIS IS WORTH KNOWING, and it inverts the stated risk: the hook comment exists to warn that the commit most likely to mis-resolve a generated artifact is ungated. In fact it is the CLEAN auto-merge that is ungated, and the conflicted merge -- the one where a human is hand-editing files and most likely to hand-resolve something generated -- is gated. So the gap is real but it is the opposite shape from the warning, and anyone relying on that comment to decide whether to run the gate by hand after an absorption is reasoning from a claim that does not hold in the conflicted case. Run it by hand anyway on a clean auto-merge; do not be surprised when it runs itself on a conflicted one. SEPARATE AND UNCHANGED: post-merge remains advisory-only because the merge commit already exists by the time it can see anything, which is the real reason the generated-artifact hazard survives.
